payload.title: CUDA to HGGC porting map (sailify + hggc-samples)
payload.summary: PPU programs are written in HGGC (HeteroGeneous General-purpose Computing) and built with `hgcc`. HGGC is close to CUDA but not identical, and the runtime reports a borrowed `sm_89`, so NVIDIA-derived assumptions must be checked rather than assumed. `sailify/sailify/cuda_to_ppu_mappings.py` is the authoritative symbol-level translation table, derived by scanning the PPU SDK headers: `cudaStream_t` -> `hggcStream_t`, `cudaError_t` -> `hggcError_t`, and the `cublas`/`cudnn` families -> `acblas`/`acdnn`. `hggc-samples` holds the official SAIL 2.1 samples, including `Samples/3_HGGC_Features/bf16_tensor_cell_gemm`. Sources: `reference-projects/sailify`, `reference-projects/hggc-samples`.

sections.heading: Symbol translation table
sections.gist: `sailify/sailify/cuda_to_ppu_mappings.py` maps CUDA types, APIs, and headers to their HGGC counterparts; check any CUDA symbol here before assuming it exists.

sections.heading: Library renames
sections.gist: The math libraries are renamed, not merely wrapped: cublas/cudnn/curand/cufft/cusparse/cusolver -> acblas/acdnn/acrand/acfft/acsparse/acsolver, NCCL -> pccl, NVTX -> hgtx.

sections.heading: Idiomatic samples
sections.gist: `hggc-samples/Samples/3_HGGC_Features/bf16_tensor_cell_gemm` shows the intended bf16 tensor-cell usage; `Common/helper_hggc.h` shows the expected error-checking idiom.

sections.heading: Borrowed sm_89
sections.gist: The runtime reports sm_89, so arch-gated CUDA code paths may select an Ada branch that does not describe this part. Gate on PPU macros (`USE_PPU`, `__HGGC_ARCH__`) instead.
